label: Customers over a store
description: How the customer port is met when the customers are kept rather than fetched: the six data graphs read and write one collection through @storage, and the business graphs are the same ones the REST binding uses -- which is the point of a port.

register.description: The data graph that stores the customer and its method’s latest as one transaction.

update.description: The business graph that loads the customer, lays the change over them, and keeps the result whole.

removeMany.description: The business graph that fans one removal out per id and waits for all of them.

submit.description: The business graph that attributes and records.

registerAll.description: The business graph that records the batch as one transaction: every draft or none.

list.description: The business graph that routes on the filter.

digest.description: The business graph that composes the digest.

import.description: The business graph that reads the file and submits each row.

export.description: The business graph that lists and writes the file.

prepare.description: Create the collections the store declares, and leave alone any that are there. The startup step names this operation, so what a tree prepares is what its project.json says it prepares.

backfill.description: The business graph that reads every record as it stands and repairs each one.

listRaw.description: A store holds only what this tree wrote, so there is nothing that predates what a customer means here: the walk starts empty and the backfill writes nothing.
